scenario.name: CISA ICS-ALERT-10-196-01, Symantec Dossier & MITRE ICS — SIMATIC STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll Interception & S7comm PLC Logic Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a precision centrifuge hall where engineers program high-speed spinning controllers through a single glass translation booth. An intruder secretly replaces the official glass translator with a double-agent imposter who passes routine messages along cleanly, slips hidden speed-tampering instructions down the cable into the spinning controllers, and then lies back through the glass whenever engineers inspect the machines, until an independent auditor taps the raw copper cable and catches the size mismatch. In this scenario (T1574.001, CISA ICS-ALERT-10-196-01, Symantec Dossier & MITRE ICS, SIMATIC STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll Interception & S7comm PLC Logic Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: engineering Workstation STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll, then s7comm Port 102 PLC Block Download, then s7comm Upload Block Readback Spoofing. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Engineering Workstation STEP 7 s7otbxdx.dll, then S7comm Port 102 PLC Block Download, then S7comm Upload Block Readback Spoofing, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 7 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.subtitle: Execution (T1059 - Command and Scripting Interpreter)

stages.title: Stage 3: S7comm Upload Block (0x1D) Readback Spoofing & Offline Checksum Verification
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1564 - Hide Artifacts)
stages.description: When a suspicious engineer opens the console to compare the live controller against the clean master blueprint, the double-agent translator intercepts the readback and holds up a fake photocopy showing normal code, until a clean auditor taps the wire directly and spots that the real packet traveling over the cable is seven times larger than what the screen claims. When an operator opens SIMATIC Manager to compare online PLC blocks with the offline project, the s7otbxdx.dll wrapper intercepts s7ag_read_szl and s7ag_bub_read_var_seg calls to hide the injected FC blocks, requiring defenders to perform a clean-boot workstation verification or direct network capture of S7comm Function 0x1D (Upload Block) (logged in Zeek ICS Event 29 with ForensicDiscrepancy=Wire S7comm OB1 size , 2,940 bytes != STEP 7 GUI displayed size , 412 bytes, InterceptedApiCall=s7otbxdx.dll!s7ag_bub_read_var_seg , User-Mode Readback Filter, RemediationAction=Restore PLC memory card from verified golden backup after replacing s7otbxdx.dll so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ s7comm port=102 func=0x1D (Upload Block) OB1 wire_bytes=2940 gui_displayed_bytes=412 / ⇠#3 RESP 29) from Node ③ (#3 s7otbxdx.dll API Wrapper) to Node ④ (#4 PLC CPU 315-2 / 417 (:102)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Profibus Frequency Converter Bus).

steps.simpleExplanation: Over ISO-on-TCP (RFC 1006 port 102), the wrapper library checks attached System Data Blocks (SDBs) for specific Profibus CP 342-5 / drive signatures (7050h / 9500h) and transmits S7comm Function 0x1A (Request Download) and 0x1B (Download Block) telegrams writing organization blocks OB1 and cyclic interrupt OB35 (logged in Zeek ICS Event 102 with Protocol=Siemens S7comm over ISO-on-TCP , Port 102, S7FunctionCode=0x1B , Download Block to PLC RAM/EPROM, TargetBlocks=OB1 , Main Sweep, OB35 , 100ms Cyclic Interrupt, FC1865..FC1874 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes tshark -r step7_plc_traffic.pcap -Y "s7comm.param.func == 0x1a || s7comm.param.func == 0x1b" -T fields -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e s7comm.param.filename (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , tshark -r step7_plc_traffic.pcap -Y "s7comm.param.func == 0x1a || s7comm.param.func == 0x1b" so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1059 during "S7comm Port 102 PLC Block Download , OB1, OB35 & System Data Block SDB" , Over ISO-on-TCP , RFC 1006 port 102, the wrapper library checks attached System Data Blocks , SDBs for specific Profibus CP 342-5 / drive signatures , 7050h / 9500h and transmits S7comm Function 0x1A , Request Download and 0x1B , Download Block telegrams writing organization blocks OB1 and cyclic interrupt OB35 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). steps.plainTitle: S7comm Upload Block (0x1D) Readback Spoofing & Offline Checksum Verification
steps.storyAnalogy: When a suspicious engineer opens the console to compare the live controller against the clean master blueprint, the double-agent translator intercepts the readback and holds up a fake photocopy showing normal code, until a clean auditor taps the wire directly and spots that the real packet traveling over the cable is seven times larger than what the screen claims.
steps.simpleExplanation: When an operator opens SIMATIC Manager to compare online PLC blocks with the offline project, the s7otbxdx.dll wrapper intercepts s7ag_read_szl and s7ag_bub_read_var_seg calls to hide the injected FC blocks, requiring defenders to perform a clean-boot workstation verification or direct network capture of S7comm Function 0x1D (Upload Block) (logged in Zeek ICS Event 29 with ForensicDiscrepancy=Wire S7comm OB1 size , 2,940 bytes != STEP 7 GUI displayed size , 412 bytes, InterceptedApiCall=s7otbxdx.dll!s7ag_bub_read_var_seg , User-Mode Readback Filter, RemediationAction=Restore PLC memory card from verified golden backup after replacing s7otbxdx.dll so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
